Visconti of Milan.fact: Here, another family member was present in the second half of the 12th century as the castellan (custos) of the local archiepiscopal fortress.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: In 1142, _____ III confirmed the investiture in a diploma released to Guido in Ulm
Visconti of Milan.fact: In 1142, King Conrad III confirmed the investiture in a diploma released to Guido in Ulm.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: A second _____, son of Guido, is attested in the documentary sources between 1134 and 1192
Visconti of Milan.fact: A second Ottone, son of Guido, is attested in the documentary sources between 1134 and 1192. The primary role of Ottone in the political life of the Milanese commune emerges in the period of the confrontation with Frederick Barbarossa: his name is the first to be cited, March 1, 1162, in the group of Milanese leaders who surrendered to the emperor after the capitulation of the city that took place in the previous weeks.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: In 1247, _____ was succeeded by his nephew Martino Della Torre
Visconti of Milan.fact: The Della Torre family progressively acquired power in Milan after 1240, when Pagano Della Torre assumed the leadership of the Credenza di Sant'Ambrogio, a political party with a popular base. In 1247, Pagano was succeeded by his nephew Martino Della Torre.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: In 1264, _____ left his office, leaving the Della Torre family members as the sole rulers of Milan
Visconti of Milan.fact: At the end of 1263, Della Torre forces, with the support of Oberto Pallavicino, dislodged him from Arona. In 1264, Pallavicino left his office, leaving the Della Torre family members as the sole rulers of Milan.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: Under the guidance of _____, brother of Martino and his successor after 1263, the Della Torre party took advantage of the favor of Charles of Anjou
Visconti of Milan.fact: Under the guidance of Filippo Della Torre, brother of Martino and his successor after 1263, the Della Torre party took advantage of the favor of Charles of Anjou.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: Francesco Della Torre led the _____ expedition, which ended in 1266 with the defeat of Manfred of Sicily, son of Frederick II, in the Battle of Benevento
Visconti of Milan.fact: Francesco Della Torre led the Milanese expedition, which ended in 1266 with the defeat of Manfred of Sicily, son of Frederick II, in the Battle of Benevento.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: In 1266, trying to take advantage of the favorable moment, the _____ advocated their cause against the Visconti in a consistory held by Pope Clement IV in Viterbo and attended by archbishop Ottone
Visconti of Milan.fact: Francesco Della Torre led the Milanese expedition, which ended in 1266 with the defeat of Manfred of Sicily, son of Frederick II, in the Battle of Benevento. Charles of Anjou became the new King of Sicily, having an indirect rule (exercised through the Della Torre) on Milan.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: Moreover, in 1268, _____ IV died, initiating a period of papal vacancy that left the dispositions in favor of Ottone without practical consequences
Visconti of Milan.fact: Moreover, in 1268, Clement IV died, initiating a period of papal vacancy that left the dispositions in favor of Ottone without practical consequences.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: The defeat and execution of _____ in Naples in 1268 meant the definitive end of the Hohenstaufen threat to Milan
Visconti of Milan.fact: At the end of 1266, the German princes decided to support Conradin, the last Hohenstaufen member, to recover the domains in southern Italy lost to the Anjou house after the defeat of Benevento. The defeat and execution of Conradin in Naples in 1268 meant the definitive end of the Hohenstaufen threat to Milan.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: The Visconti defeated the _____ army in the decisive Battle of Desio on 21 January 1277, opening the way for Ottone to enter Milan
Visconti of Milan.fact: The Visconti defeated the Della Torre army in the decisive Battle of Desio on 21 January 1277, opening the way for Ottone to enter Milan. Napoleone, son of Pagano, was arrested with other Della Torre family members.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: Looking for a reconciliation, he transferred the power to his eldest son _____ and left Milan for the Augustinian monastery of Crescenzago, where he died in 1322
Visconti of Milan.fact: Looking for a reconciliation, he transferred the power to his eldest son Galeazzo and left Milan for the Augustinian monastery of Crescenzago, where he died in 1322. After Matteo's death, Galeazzo associated his brothers, Marco, Luchino, Stefano, and Giovanni (a cleric), in the inherited domains' controls.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage

Visconti of Milan.fact: However, in the Battle of Parabiago, 1339, he was defeated by an army led by Azzone and backed by his uncles, Luchino and Giovanni.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: After Luchino died in 1349, archbishop _____ remained alone in power and recalled Matteo II, Bernabò, and Galeazzo II in Milan
Visconti of Milan.fact: Azzone died in 1339 without sons, and the power passed to Luchino and Giovanni (since 1342, archbishop of Milan). After Luchino died in 1349, archbishop Giovanni remained alone in power and recalled Matteo II, Bernabò, and Galeazzo II in Milan.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: Violante, daughter of _____, married in 1368 Lionel of Antwerp, Duke of Clarence, the third son of King Edward III of England
Visconti of Milan.fact: Bernabò and Galeazzo II extended the Visconti relationships to several European noble dynasties through their children's marriages. In 1360, Gian Galeazzo, son of Galeazzo II, married Isabella of Valois, daughter of King John II of France.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: After her husband's death, only a few months after the marriage, in 1377, _____ married Secondotto, Marquess of Montferrat
Visconti of Milan.fact: Violante, daughter of Galeazzo II, married in 1368 Lionel of Antwerp, Duke of Clarence, the third son of King Edward III of England. After her husband's death, only a few months after the marriage, in 1377, Violante married Secondotto, Marquess of Montferrat.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage

Visconti of Milan.fact: In 1395, for 100,000 florins, Gian Galeazzo obtained the Duke of Milan's title from the King Wenceslaus IV of Bohemia. After a short disease, the plague or gout, Gian Galeazzo died on 3 September 1402.

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage

Visconti of Milan.fact: In the same year, his brother Filippo Maria married the widow of Facino Cane, the 42-year-old Beatrice of Tenda, taking advantage of a testamentary disposition in favor of any Visconti that would have married her. Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: After an _____-Spanish army defeated France in the Battle of Pavia in 1525, a Sforza, Francesco II, assumed rule in Milan again

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
Visconti of Milan.question: After his defeat in the _____ of San Ruffillo in 1361, Bernabò finally came to terms with the loss of Bologna

Visconti of Milan.subject: Indian Heritage
